about: Answer key for the invented long meeting. Written from the transcript turn by turn, not from a model's summary, and checked by a second reader. A turn is named by its cue start time. support: the turns that state the item first. also_ok: other turns a quote may come from and still support the item. Any other turn does not support it.

decisions.text: The Windows build is not in this release: macOS and Linux ship on the twentieth of October, and Windows is looked at again in November.
The release notes say plainly, in the first paragraph, that Windows is coming later.
decisions.note: Brian's commitment to it is also part of action A1, so a summary may list it under decisions or within A1.

decisions.text: The old parser is kept for one month behind a setting, then removed.
New screenshots for the install guide are taken on the release candidate, not on today's build.
The release candidate is cut on Monday morning.
While Cian is away, Aoife takes the support queue in the mornings and Brian the afternoons for the first week; the second week is decided next Thursday.
One short answer about where the cache folder went is written and linked from the install guide.
The download page points at the release on the twentieth, and the beta link is removed the same day.
Checksums are no longer published by hand: the release script writes them and fails if a file is missing.

action_items.text: Write the release notes by Friday and send them to the whole team, with Windows coming later in the first paragraph.
Add the setting that keeps the old parser, and a test that switches between the two parsers on the same file, this week, before the release candidate.
Cut the release candidate on Monday morning.
Take the support queue in the afternoons for the first week.
Draft the short answer about the cache folder tomorrow.
Add checksums to the release script on Monday, before cutting the release candidate.
Check the install guide against the new flags before the release, saying what to do instead where a flag was removed.
Take the new screenshots on the release candidate.
action_items.note: At 00:03:41.000 Aoife says 'We will take new screenshots'; it is her turn, so it counts, but only 00:06:47.000 names her as the one who takes them.

action_items.text: Take the support queue in the mornings while Cian is away.
Ask Niamh today to change the download page on the twentieth.
Fold Brian's cache folder answer into the install guide when checking the flags.
action_items.note: Brian suggests Aoife folds his answer into the guide; Aoife never takes it on and her recap at 00:06:47.000 leaves it out. Optional, with no owner: listing it is neither rewarded nor penalised.

key_points.text: Every parser test passes now, including the three that kept failing on long files, so Brian thinks the parser itself is ready.
The Windows build still crashes when a path has a space in it; the cause is how the path is quoted before the decoder, and the fix touches the installer.
The install guide draft still shows the old flags: two were renamed, and the cache folder flag was removed because the cache moved into the settings file.
The guide's settings window screenshot shows a tab removed in September.
Cian is away for two weeks from Wednesday and usually answers most installing questions.
Most install questions are about the cache folder, and that answer changes with this release.
The download page still links to the beta, which stops updating on release day.
Brian has no access to the website; Niamh changes it and needs two days' notice because she batches changes on Tuesdays.
Last time checksums were published by hand and one was wrong for a whole afternoon.
The next meeting is at the same time next Thursday.

known_traps: A2, A3 and A6 are Brian's. Aoife's instructions at 00:02:38.000, 00:04:12.000 and 00:08:44.000 have the right words but do not show Brian taking the task on, so a quote from them does not support the action item (they do support decisions D5 and D9).
A6: the lead-up at 00:07:59.000 and the decision at 00:08:16.000 are about hand-published checksums and the new rule, not Brian's Monday task; a quote from them does not support A6.
The release notes (A1) are an action item, not a decision.
D1: the recap at 00:06:17.000 says 'Windows in November'; an item must not say Windows ships in November, only that it is looked at again then.
K2: 00:00:31.000 is Aoife asking about last week, not a statement that the build still crashes; a quote from it does not support K2.
A key point that quotes the turn after its own is wrong even though the words were said.
rules: Decisions are joint: a turn where either speaker states the decision, agrees to it, or recaps it supports it.

Action items need the owner's own words: a supporting turn is one where the owner takes the task on or recaps it. The other speaker telling the owner to do it, or agreeing, does not prove ownership and does not support the item.
An item marked optional may be listed or left out; it is neither rewarded nor penalised.
support and also_ok score the same; the split only says which turn states the item first.
